19.description: The committee considered a $6.24 million full reconstruction of the 51st Street and Millar Avenue intersection to improve safety and traffic flow. It would restrict left turns for adjacent businesses.

chips.text: Defeated
1 for, 5 against
Councillor Donauer noted 'impact on businesses' was removed from evaluation criteria.
Businesses like Tim Hortons, McDonald's, and Co-op would lose left-turn access.
Staff stated a raised median is essential, not seeing alternatives for left turns.
Staff could not estimate business traffic loss from restricted left turns.
Adjacent businesses opposed Option C due to restricted access and parking loss.
Councillor Pierce would avoid businesses if left turns were restricted.
Project would require removal of 3 city and 28 private trees.
Staff promised to replace removed trees, at a minimum, if the project proceeds.

20.description: A committee deferred an $8.47 million plan for new pathways on both sides of Millar Avenue, seeking more engagement with affected businesses.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Dunner felt public engagement was hostile and did not reflect business concerns.
Business owners face parking loss due to public right-of-way reclamation.
Committee deferred staff recommendation for more business engagement.
Will the new pathways be used, given current low traffic?
Businesses expressed concern over parking loss and tree removal impacts.
Project requires removal of 197 trees; replacement plan details are pending.
Administration promised to work with businesses on parking loss mitigation.

22.description: The committee recommends an overpass design for the 8th Street CPKC rail crossing, funded by developer contributions, with construction targeted for 2030.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Staff clarified West Road's 8th Street access will close, but Taylor Street access remains.
Current and future Homewood sector neighborhoods will fund the project.
Public engagement showed broad support for the overpass with noise mitigation requests.
Sound walls will be included in the budget for noise mitigation.

21.description: The committee recommends repealing the outdated Helicopter Services policy and updating the Flypasts and Parachute Jumps policy to include helicopter approvals and municipal non-objection for balloon festivals.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Affects applicants for helicopter takeoffs/landings and balloon festivals.

9.description: Saskatoon is implementing continuous improvement in fleet services and warehousing, focusing on safety, productivity, and space utilization. This initiative will expand to other city departments.

chips.text: Councillor Dunner thanked administration for work on continuous improvement, savings
Fleet services and supply chain management staff are directly involved in improvements.
Administration will complete ongoing projects, sustain improvements

18.description: Saskatoon is implementing continuous improvement in fleet services, focusing on safety, efficiency, and employee engagement to find savings and improve operations.

chips.text: Received as information
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Donauer praised employee engagement for safety, savings, and sustainability.
Fleet services and supply chain management staff are directly affected.
The continuous improvement program will expand to other city departments.
Administration will report quantifiable benefits and savings in future reports.
